messages:
Amelia: heads-up — after the v2.14 rollout (canary -> 25%) we started seeing p95 jump from ~180ms to ~700ms for short text-gen calls (seq len 64). Noticing customer escalations and internal alerts.
Javier: saw the same in dashboards ~5m ago. p99 spikes to 1.2s. Any correlation with new kernel selection changes in this rollout?
Amelia: rollout included runtime image runtime:v2.14.1 and new batching heuristic (dynamic-prefix-batching). Canary was 10% earlier, we moved to 25% at 12:09UTC (deploy bot message).
oncall-bot: ALERT: latency_slo_p95 breach on service=runtime-global region=us-west-2 value=720ms threshold=300ms at 2026-03-15T12:18:02Z
Ryan: quick check — are these all on a single GPU type? prometheus shows most from g4dn-like nodes in us-west-2. Also a subset looks like cache miss rate increased.
Sasha: I pulled a few raw request traces. Many of the slow traces show repeated KV cache misses and a sudden spike in `decode_token()` time. attaching snippet:
```
trace id=tx-7b9f
service runtime
span: batch_wait 82ms
span: kv_lookup 134ms (miss)
span: kernel_launch 420ms
span: decode_token 210ms
```
Amelia: repro steps from Support: small prompt (<=64), model redwood-3b-quant, single request. They provided curl with x-redwood-trace header.
SupportBot: forwarded customer thread — multiple customers reporting higher latencies after ~12:10UTC. Billing/quotas unaffected.
Javier: can we roll the canary back to 10% while we investigate? That buys time.
Ryan: agreed. propose: 1) drop traffic back to 10% for runtime:v2.14.1 2) enable fallback to runtime:v2.13 for affected routes 3) collect flamegraphs from healthy vs slow instances.
Sasha: I'm running `kubectl logs -lapp=runtime -c inference --since=5m` on the canary pool now. seeing `TF_CUDA_WARN: kernel timeout` occasionally on a node (node-id i-0c...).
Amelia: interesting — we didn't change CUDA kernels explicitly but kernel selection was updated to prefer f32 path for small batches. Could be causing more kernel launches.
Javier: doing a bisect on the release commits to find the regression. suspect commit `b9f2c4` (batch heuristic tweak) or `c1a3de` (kernel selector default change). Will run `git bisect run ./scripts/run-latency-check.sh` across the release branch.
Ryan: while bisect runs, mitigate: scaling rule — temporarily increase min-workers on canary pool by 2 to spread load, and patch runtime config to prefer older kernel path (`KERNEL_STRATEGY=compat`) via pod rollout.
Sasha: patched KERNEL_STRATEGY env on the canary daemonset, doing rolling restart. verifying traces... immediate p95 drop to ~210ms on restarted pods.
Amelia: that points to kernel selector change as the main culprit. Good find. But we should still finish bisect to be sure.
Javier: git bisect completed: culprit is `c1a3de` — kernel selector default changed. Repro script shows single-process cold-start kernel launch time increased ~350ms per request.
Ryan: decision: rollback runtime:v2.14.1 to v2.14.0 on canary and schedule a patch that reverts kernel selector default, add better telemetry to compare kernel launch times, and add a canary smoke test that runs synthetic short-request loop.
Amelia: I've issued rollback to 10% -> 0% then back to 10% targeting v2.14.0 for user traffic. oncall-bot: note the change in deployment channel.
oncall-bot: DEPLOY: rollback runtime:v2.14.1 -> runtime:v2.14.0 initiated by Amelia at 2026-03-15T12:33:44Z
SupportBot: forwarded update to impacted customers: we reverted the canary and are investigating root cause; apologies for the disruption.
Sasha: created a quick patch that leaves new selector behind a feature flag `ENABLE_NEW_KERNEL_SELECTOR=false` and added `kernel_launch_ms` histogram with labels (node_type, model, batch_size). PR at https://repo/reds/runtime/pull/4123
Javier: we should add a step in the rollout playbook: after changing kernel selection, run `smoke-short-gen` (script) against canary with 1k requests and assert p95 < 300ms.
Amelia: noted. Also we should update the rollouts dashboard to graph kernel_launch_ms and kv_cache_hit_rate side-by-side.
Ryan: next steps: 1) merge the feature-flag PR, 2) run canary with the smoke test (automated), 3) only ramp if both p95 and kernel_launch_ms look stable for 30m. I'll own the smoke test job.
Amelia: thanks team. I'll draft a short postmortem and customer note. Tagging for a quick sync at 13:15UTC to finalize remediation and release plan. :thumbsup:
Javier: +1.
Sasha: leaving logs and flamegraphs in the incident folder /artifacts/1772301123/ — includes `perf` and `nvprof` dumps.
Amelia: closing loop for now — rollback succeeded and p95 returned to baseline on canary traffic. We'll keep on-call monitoring while patch lands.
Ryan: adding retro action: tighter gating for kernel changes, and synthetic load that stresses small-batch fast-paths.
Amelia: thanks — nice rapid detection and rollback.
